Check the code that was just written against the following guidelines and report
violations along with recommended fixes.

## General guidelines

- This project is built with Biff, a web framework. There are specific ways you
  should do things in Biff that may not match the way you would do them in a
  vanilla Clojure project. If you had to introduce a new pattern in your code,
  check the current codebase and the biff documentation at `.biff/docs/` to
  ensure your code matches established patterns. If `.biff/docs/` isn't present,
  run `clojure -M:run init`.

- Some feedback here may be written for a specific library like biff.sqlite. If
  the project isn't using the library but they are using an alternative, see if
  the guideline is relevant to the alternative.

## Project structure

- `model` namespaces expose biff.core modules that mostly contain biff.graph
  resolvers. Resolvers related to a particular database entity should be grouped
  in a file named for that entity, e.g. `module/user.clj`. You can introduce
  additional `model` namespaces (i.e. not named for a particular database
  entity) if needed; try to keep any additional resolvers grouped cohesively.

- `app` namespaces contain ring handlers for rendering web pages, including
  internal endpoints needed by those web pages. It's common to have one `app`
  module per page.

- `work` namespaces contain biff.background queues and scheduled tasks.

- `uicomp` namespaces contain shared UI components that require inputs from
  biff.graph. These are exposed as biff.graph resolvers that return either
  hiccup vectors or functions that return hiccup vectors.

- If the app has an external API, those routes can go in `api` namespaces.

- `model`, `app`, `work`, `uicomp` and `api` namespaces are all "module"
  namespaces and should expose their functionality via biff.core modules.

- Module namespaces should only be required by the main `modules.clj` file.
  Module namespaces should not require each other. Shared functions should go
  under a `lib` namespace. If a function is only needed in one place, it's
  typically better to define it there as a private function instead of in `lib`.

- Derived data should typically be written as a biff.graph resolver (in `model`)
  instead of as a shared function (in `lib`).

- Database queries should almost always be encapsulated within biff.graph
  resolvers in `model`. Any code outside `model` that runs a database query is a
  red flag, especially if it's in `app`.

- Try to avoid creating namespaces with `util` in the name. Functions should be
  grouped into namespaces with more semantic names.

- Try to keep namespaces to around 500 lines at most.

## Library usage

- Keep state in the system map. e.g. if you need an atom, you can make a
  biff.core module like `{:biff.core/init {:com.example/my-atom (atom {})}}`.

- If the project uses biff.fx and biff.sqlite, then the
  `:biff.sqlite.fx/authorized-write` fx handler should typically be used for
  writes that are initiated by a user. The `:biff.sqlite/authorize` key
  (typically passed to the sqlite module) should be set to a function which has
  been updated to match the application's schema. In general, the authorization
  rules should allow users to write records they "own" without letting them
  write records they don't own. For example, a user should be able to edit their
  own settings but not other users' settings.

- Effectful functions should typically be written as biff.fx pipelines (or plain
  machines if needed), using injected parameters as needed: `:biff.fx/now`,
  `:biff.fx/random-uuid7-seq`, `:biff.fx/random-uuid4-seq`, `:biff.fx/seed`. Any
  effect not implemented as a biff.fx handler is a red flag.

- For example, biff.sqlite database queries should be done via biff.fx handlers.
  However if the project uses an immutable database like XTDB or Datomic,
  queries may be considered "pure" and don't need to go through a biff.fx
  handler as long as the function receives an immutable snapshot of the
  database.

- SQL queries should be written with HoneySQL whenever possible (e.g. by passing
  a map to a biff.sqlite fx handler).

- Always use `com.biffweb.ring/defpath` to define reitit path templates, whether
  or not they use path parameters. Paths referenced from only one file should be
  defined in that file; other paths can be defined in a shared `routes.clj`
  file.

## Tests

- Tests for a namespace should go in a namespace of the same name withe the
  `-test` suffix, e.g. tests for `com.example.lib.foo` go in
  `com.example.lib.foo-test`.

- Every biff.fx machine or pipeline should have one or more unit tests for each
  of its state functions. Call the machine/pipeline with zero arguments to get
  the state functions for testing. The tests should cover any conditional
  branches in each state function.

## Code style

- When using biff.sqlite, the columns map should separate schema entries for
  different tables with a blank line. Schema should only be broken on multiple
  lines if it's necessary to avoid lint warnings about line length. If you must
  use a line break but the entry value can fit on a single line, do that:

```
:user/example-attribute
{:type ..., :required ..., ...}
```

- Agents should not make changes to clj-kondo or cljfmt config unless directed
  by the user. If the max line length has been increased or cljfmt rules have
  been relaxed, that's a red flag.
